fact: Lesotho's action timeline lists implementing an Integrated National Digital Identity Ecosystem for 2026-2030 with MICSTI and UNICEF.

The Ministry of Home Affairs engaged AAM Consultancy to assess existing systems and develop a systems architecture and modernization framework for an integrated digital identity system, presented at a workshop from 29 June to 3 July 2026, per the Government of Lesotho.

Lesotho's Ministry of Information (MICSTI) says a pilot of the new digital/service identification system begins on 2 April 2026 with about 10,000 participants, who enrol with a valid national ID document, a registered SIM and biometric registration.
Biometric Update reports that UNICEF and the Ministry of Information (MICSTI) signed a 2026 work plan to develop an integrated national digital ID ecosystem, with Lesotho building its DPI on MOSIP.
The 2026 work plan supports development of an integrated national digital identity ecosystem, with biometric registration and continued MOSIP-based deployment.
MICSTI and the National University of Lesotho reviewed progress on MOSIP, which is to provide a secure biometric digital ID for public services.

fact: Co-Develop and FinMark Trust state that in a pilot Lesotho migrants in South Africa accessed formal remittance services using their national digital IDs, verified in real time across the border.
The Lesotho Times reports Pangea's court claim that the Ministry of Home Affairs kept relying on the national identification systems Pangea implemented through to the December 2024 termination.
UNDP reports Home Affairs says it has registered 95% of targeted citizens, approaching 1.4 million, capturing ten fingerprints and a photo, with charge-free ID issuance and continuous data update.
